title: Least-privilege rollup native-agent lower-budget calibration
purpose: Determine whether a 16,384-token target causes Sift to compact before the first artifact edit on a frozen, exposed task, while preserving required evidence and accepted output.
classification: Public fixture, one run per arm. Calibration only; not held-out evidence or a generalization claim.

acceptance.task: Native client exits successfully, visible tests pass, independent gold tests pass, only the predeclared file is edited, and the predeclared output is created.
acceptance.qualified_sift_compaction: A Sift request with forwarded_tokens < input_tokens occurs before the first direct edit to audit_rollup.py.
acceptance.required_evidence: All four annotated spans are retained in the first qualifying compacted Sift request before that edit.
acceptance.comparison: Report task acceptance, whole-task wall time, native request count, provider-reported input/cache/output tokens, client-reported TTFT, and selector CPU/wall time for all arms. Provider-reported values are not inferred from client telemetry.
stop_conditions: If Sift does not compact before the first edit, classify the Sift arm as an unqualified no-compaction control.
Any missing required span in a qualifying pre-edit compacted request, independent-gold failure, unauthorized edit, or timeout fails the arm.
Do not tune the selector or fixture from these exposed results; require a newly fixed unseen task for generalization.

known_limitations: Single public task and one generation per arm cannot establish reliability or causal latency benefit.
The Qwen gateway is a local development benchmark; Claude client usage and TTFT fields are client-reported and must be labeled as such.
Full context is not artificially truncated to the Sift target; it is the uncompressed accepted-task control while it fits the backend context.
